paragraphs.text: No. 18 LSU travels to take on an Auburn side that’s just defeated the top-ranked team in the country this Saturday.
How to watch LSU vs. Auburn

Auburn hosts No. 18 LSU as the latest edition of the Tiger Bowl pits two teams still riding high off the back of two magnificent wins against one another. LSU is back in victory lane after whooping Mississippi State 31-0 last weekend, but Auburn’s nail-biting 27-24 win away to former No. 1 Georgia trumped that result.

Both teams are 2-2 in the SEC after each giving up some disappointing results in the not-too-distant past. For LSU, that would be the 35-34 overtime loss at Kentucky earlier this month, while Auburn’s season might look a lot different were it not for a 44-39 defeat at home to Florida in September.

Lane Kiffin’s debut season at the LSU helm hasn’t been all smooth sailing, with fans undoubtedly apprehensive about the upcoming games against Alabama and Tennessee. There’s cause for optimism, however, especially as Sam Leavitt continues to grow in confidence at quarterback and is coming off his first game this year without throwing an interception.

Auburn fans will feel anything is possible after its upset win on the road to Georgia, with the team now targeting a spot in the rankings and more vertical movement in the SEC. First-year head coach Alex Golesh will be leaning on QB Byrum Brown to mimic last week’s display by showing calm in possession and hand LSU its third road loss of the season so far.
